Round 2 is done: the review found three problems, all three are fixed in separate commits, and nothing was pushed.

The verdict was BLOCKING. The rules treat any listed-constraint violation as BLOCKING, and all three break a listed rule, `PATTERN-comment-line-breaks` or `PATTERN-test-speed`.

I reviewed `git diff $(git merge-base main HEAD)..HEAD`. The build, `go vet` under every tag, and the untagged `go test ./...` all pass. I did not run the integration or tmux test tiers; only `go vet` covers those.

| Finding | Problem | Fix commit |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Two new doc comments in `tools/godocreflow/reflow_test.go` broke mid-sentence. | `a22f7d533` |
| F2 | `internal/selfreportengine/selfreport_test.go` swaps the package-level `NewGitHubClient` seam and never said why its tests run serially. | `9d953ceb4` |
| F3 | `TestSeed_WritesExpectedStatus` in `internal/loomshed/seed_test.go` had parallel subtests but no top-level `t.Parallel()`. | `89e09ad6a` |

The other two focus sweeps came back clean. No test helper is left without a caller in the files the focus named. No file names a top-level test the prune deleted or turned into a subtest.

My first scan also flagged two tests that turned out to be fine: `TestLoadConfig_ScalarKeysAndTemplateDefaults` and the two `landingshed` commit-status tables. Each already had a comment saying why it runs serially; my keyword match missed the word "serial". I took both out of the review file before fixing anything.

`golangci-lint`'s `unused` check also reports unused fields, `gate` in `prgate_test.go` and `beforeCreate` in `publish_integration_test.go`. Both exist unchanged on base, so I left them alone.

The review is `_lyx/reviews/webster/round-2-review.md` and the fixer report is `_lyx/reviews/webster/round-2-fixer-report.md`.
